result.title: ARIDA - Active railway infrastructure dataset annotation using neural network predictions
result.summary: Modern railway perception requires large comprehensive image datasets, but creating them is slowed by manual labeling, especially for track polylines and other complex infrastructure geometry. This paper presents the Active Railway Infrastructure Dataset Annotation framework, a railway-specific semi-automated pipeline that converts instance predictions from a mask scoring instance segmentation network into bounding-boxes, polygons, polylines, and paired polylines. To keep automatic track geometry annotation reliable without ground truth, it applies confidence thresholds and an unique contour-agreement quality score as an acceptance gate. An active learning loop ranks remaining images by uncertainty and adapts the number of manual queries per cycle. This is achieved through a novel quantity control mechanism, in which easy images are auto-accepted and human effort targets hard cases. Experiments on disjoint, diverse imagery and time-sequential, redundant imagery quantify effort reduction and accuracy trade-offs, achieving about two thirds reduction in the disjoint regime and up to 93% in the sequential regime. The study also provides guidance for initial label budgets and stopping to avoid over-annotation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ARIDA 铁路半自动标注流水线：将实例分割预测转换为包围盒、多边形、折线等几何标注，用置信度阈值与轮廓一致性质量分数作为验收门，并以不确定性排序的主动学习循环自适应调节每轮人工查询量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不确定性选样＋质量门控＋何时停止标注」的组合，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与 STOP 的成本收益权衡形成概念对应，可供核查；但工作面向数据标注流水线而非推理期 latent 状态，联系较远。
